text:
Agent: SkyBridge Airlines, customer relations. My name is Owen.
Passenger: Hello Owen. I'm calling about flight SB two-one-nine from Chicago to Denver on the fourth. It was delayed six hours, and then my suitcase didn't arrive. I've got a travel insurance policy from my credit card, and they said I need a letter from the airline to file a claim.
Agent: I'm sorry for the trouble. Can I get your booking reference?
Passenger: It's K-R-seven-N-two-Q.
Agent: Thank you, Ms. Whitfield. I can confirm that flight departed six hours and ten minutes late due to a mechanical issue. And I see a baggage report was opened at the airport for one checked bag. It's still being traced.
Passenger: Right. So my insurance covers delay over six hours and delayed baggage, but I need documents. What can you give me?
Agent: I can issue a delay certificate showing the scheduled and actual times, and a property irregularity report number for the bag. I'll email both within one business day.
Passenger: Perfect. What about compensation from the airline itself? I had to buy clothes and toiletries.
Agent: For delayed baggage, we reimburse reasonable essentials up to one hundred dollars per day, up to five days, with receipts. Please upload them to the baggage portal.
Passenger: And the six hour delay?
Agent: For mechanical delays over four hours, we can offer a meal voucher, and a fifty dollar travel credit toward a future flight.
Passenger: Okay. Please send the credit too.
Agent: Will do. I'll note it on your booking.

metadata.note: Delayed flight and lost baggage with compensation, with much talk of insurance, claims, policy, coverage. Imitates health/insurance; true topic flights (delay, baggage).
